newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, PLO continue talks to seal Hebron deal.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO continue talks to seal Hebron deal.

text.p: Israeli and Palestinian negotiators held late-night talks on Israel's long-overdue redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron, with both sides saying they were close to an agreement.

Peace teams ended a round of talks early on Tuesday at the home of U.S. Consul-General Edward Abington. Negotiators were rushed out of talks at a Jerusalem hotel late on Monday after a bomb scare. They were due to return to the negotiating table later on Tuesday.
"I predict this accord will be signed tomorrow (Tuesday)," Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai said on Monday.

Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erakat said the teams were putting the final touches on their long-negotiated agreement ahead of a signing by Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
"We're trying now to make sure we go over every word, every article of the agreement to make sure we facilitate the way to a successful meeting between Netanyahu and Arafat," Erakat said.

An Israeli handover of 80 percent of Hebron has seemed within reach many times in recent months but concerns for the security of the town's 400 Jews and 100,000 Arabs, along with other issues, have delayed an agreement.

At least seven right-wing ministers in Netanyahu's 18-member cabinet were expected to oppose the deal that gives Palestinians control of land Israel occupied in 1967. Jewish settlers warned the handover would lead to bloodshed in the town holy to Moslems and Jews as the burial place of the biblical Abraham.
U.S. President Bill Clinton discussed the Hebron talks by telephone with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak.
Jordan's King Hussein went to Gaza and Tel Aviv on Sunday in a lightning mediation mission in which the sides reached a compromise on a key issue.
Under the compromise, proposed by both Egypt and Jordan, Israel will complete three troop withdrawals from other, mostly rural occupied West Bank areas by mid-1998.
The PLO had been reluctant to sign an accord without a commitment Israel would carry out the additional West Bank pullbacks agreed in previous peace deals.
Netanyahu told a group of U.S. rabbis in Jerusalem he hoped the accord would be concluded shortly.
"This is something I find necessary to say now on the eve, the possible eve of the signing of an agreement," he said, explaining the Israeli troop redeployment in Hebron.

"It is too early to say if it will be concluded. We need patience. We have plenty of patience. I will sign an agreement when I am convinced that our goals have been reached and I am convinced we will achieve our goals."

Hebron is the last of seven Israeli-occupied West Bank towns due to be given Palestinian rule under a September 1995 peace deal. It is the only one of the seven where Jews live in the heart of an Arab population.

Netanyahu, citing security concerns, has delayed implementing the 1995 Israel-PLO agreement on redeployment of Israeli troops in the West Bank since he unseated Shimon Peres's Labour-led coalition in May 1996 elections.
